messages:
mike_support: Heads-up — Acme (account acct_784) reported sudden 401s and high P95 latency. They say traffic that normally hits us-east-1 is routing to eu-west-1 and failing auth.
customer_jane: Confirmed — started ~10:42 UTC. Single API key, started getting 401s and much slower responses.
lia_support: Any request-id or sample trace?
mike_support: Request-id: r-0a3f5c9b. Curl sent by customer:
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer sk.acme..." https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"x"}'
```
ashley_sre: @mike_support thanks. Looking at routing logs — origin probe for us-east returned intermittent 504s around 10:41-10:43. Traffic was shifted by the smart-router to fallback region (eu-west).
oliver_oncall: Deploy-bot shows a healthcheck config change at 10:40:55: `probe_ttl` lowered from 30s -> 10s in canary; rolled to 3 nodes in us-east. :eyes:
deploy-bot: rollback of canary triggered automatically at 10:44:03 due to error budget breach.
jun_platform: That TTL change can make transient packet loss look like a hard failure and trigger failover. If a customer uses region-bounded signed tokens (we do in some SDKs), auth will fail when served from another region.
mike_support: Customer says they use standard hosted API key — are keys region-scoped?
ashley_sre: Not usually, but we do have a per-region token flag for some legacy orgs. Checking account metadata now.
lia_support: Also seeing a billing spike in their dashboard — looks like retries + cross-region routing increased token-checks and cache misses.
ashley_sre: Repro steps we used: 1) On canary, set probe_ttl=10s 2) Simulate SYN loss to health endpoint 3) Router marks region unhealthy in <20s 4) Traffic routes to eu-west, signed token validation fails for Org legacy flag -> 401.
mike_support: Customer requested timeline and mitigation. They've opened a case; need ETA to restore stable routing and confirm no lingering auth tokens are invalid.
jun_platform: Mitigation plan: a) pin their account to us-east route for 1h (manual routing override) b) revert probe_ttl change and redeploy canary with gradual ramp c) add a safety floor so probe_ttl never <20s for primary regions.
oliver_oncall: Doing manual pin now. Routing override applied at 10:49 UTC.
lia_support: Notifying customer that routing pinned and we're rolling back config.
mike_support: Customer acknowledged and will monitor. They also want root cause in incident writeup.
ashley_sre: I'll draft the postmortem entry and include reproducible steps + config diff. Assigning follow-ups: JUN for routing policy fix, ASHLEY for postmortem, OLIVER for automation to prevent low-ttl canaries.
mike_support: Thanks all. Marking incident INC-1792123456 for tracking.
customer_jane: Thanks team — appreciate the quick pin. We'll report if anything else pops up. :thumbsup:
